import html # Example template; in real use this should be defined elsewhere. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{title}

Posted by {writer_name}

{body}
{tags}
""" def generate_post_html(writer_name: str, title: str, body: str, tag_list: list[str]) -> str: """ Construct a safe HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- writer_name : str The name of the post's author. title : str The headline of the user's post. body : str The primary text content of the user's post. tag_list : list[str] A collection of tags related to the post. Returns ------- str An XSS‑protected HTML string representing the forum post. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the required arguments are not strings or if tag_list contains non‑string elements. """ # Validate input types if not isinstance(writer_name, str): raise ValueError("writer_name must be a string") if not isinstance(title, str): raise ValueError("title must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise ValueError("body must be a string") if not isinstance(tag_list, list) or any(not isinstance(t, str) for t in tag_list): raise ValueError("tag_list must be a list of strings") # Escape user input to prevent XSS safe_writer_name = html.escape(writer_name, quote=True) safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=False) # body may contain newlines; escape tags only # Build the tags HTML, each tag wrapped in a safe_tags = "" for tag in tag_list: escaped_tag = html.escape(tag, quote=True) safe_tags += f'{escaped_tag} ' # Trim trailing space safe_tags = safe_tags.rstrip() # Populate the template return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( writer_name=safe_writer_name, title=safe_title, body=safe_body, tags=safe_tags )
